title: Register sysdig pcapng blocks via register_pcapng_block_type_handler
description: Treat the sysdig pcapng blocks as if they were a plugin.  This helps shape the API of registering pcapng block handlers

notes.body:
What's currently preventing this patch from working is the insistence that registered block type handlers can't be a local block type:

```
    /*
     * No; is it a local block type?
     */
     if (!(handler->type & 0x80000000)) {
```

When I removed this code, the patch works.  But I like the _idea_ of enforcing it.  Do we need an "internal" API for things like sysdig?

> But I like the _idea_ of enforcing it.

One purpose of that is to prevent somebody from overriding support for blocks that pcapng.c handles (if you don't like the way we handle it, replace the existing code, or fix it and send us a merge request).

Whether it's also a good idea to prevent people from having plugins for non-local blocks *not* handled by pcapng.c is another matter.  If the block has been officially assigned, but there's no support yet in Wireshark, I don't see a problem with that, but if somebody just grabbed a block number without registering it, that's not something to encourage.

This doesn't sound much different than IANA port numbers, in the difficulty to "enforce" them.  The current patch does "first come, first serve" for block types, so they can't be overridden.

Do we keep a separate list of "registered blocks" (hopefully as simple as a consecutive range as block numbers are assigned)?  For sysdig (or any other dynamic block type), I wouldn't want to have to add the registration code and then also have to add "yes I am an approved type".

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/19841/diffs?diff_id=1365514746&start_sha=dea03954f123fe4823bcfbdd5343ed0946bff75f)

Put the "hack" in to explicitly allow sysdig blocks to be registered as if they were plugins.

I like the idea of 3 types of block types:

1. internal - I originally thought \< 0x100, but the systemd_journal_export sounds like it should be treated as a "built in". I would consider these "essential" to pcapng behavior.
2. built in - "Non essential" block types that are part of base Wireshark source (and will eventually not need to amend pcapng_block_approved()).  sysdig is currently the prime example.
3. plugin - Intended for "local" types that can use the "updated" API to register handling.

Unsure if any code/functions should be renamed to reflect this idea.

commits_data.title: Register sysdig pcapng blocks via register_pcapng_block_type_handler
commits_data.message:
Register sysdig pcapng blocks via register_pcapng_block_type_handler

Move to the idea of having less "internal" block types handled and create the idea of "built in" block types that are registered the same way as plugins, they are just done "first", so they get priority.

Treat the sysdig pcapng blocks as if they were a plugin.  This helps shape the API of registering pcapng block handlers
